A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Internal Confidence research, with matching authors, method, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original uncertainty-estimation and runtime results on TriviaQA, SciQ, and GSM8K, alongside adaptive RAG, model cascading, and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds benchmark outcomes in Table A2 and decision-center analyses in Figures A4–A6.

M1.justification: The P(YES) computation, weighted aggregation, and default fixed decision center remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds a TruthfulQA-specific adaptation that learns the decision center from 100 validation samples; v2 discussed center optimization but used the fixed center.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 and Table A2 add SimpleQA factual questions, MuSiQue multihop reasoning, and TruthfulQA questions targeting misconceptions. The original three datasets and adaptive-inference tasks remain, substantially broadening evaluated data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and A1 expand the evaluated answer-level comparator set from five to eight methods by adding Maximum Sequence Probability (MSP), CCP, and EV Laplacian across the original datasets. Table 1 retains its query-level comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes Phi prompting from three shots to two, although Table 1 remains numerically identical and no rerun is established. The added TruthfulQA evaluation introduces center selection using a 100-sample held-out validation set. Existing model sizes, correctness criteria, and principal dataset splits remain unchanged; AUC is clarified as AUROC.

E4.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a systematic examination of decision-center locations across models and tasks, illustrated by Figures A4–A6, extending v2's single illustrative heatmap analysis. This directly examines the fixed-center assumption. Existing calibration, in-context-example, and locality analyses are retained; conflicting captions limit precise attribution of the new heatmaps.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both describe random selection of in-context examples and otherwise retain point-estimate reporting; the added results introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table A2 adds extensive results on three new benchmarks, with a learned center used for TruthfulQA. New MSP results change the GSM8K ranking: 68.5 AUROC versus Internal Confidence's unchanged 66.8. Table 2 also changes Lexical Similarity runtime from 22.3 to 170.3 seconds and its speedup comparison from 74× to 567×. Table 1 is unchanged.

T1.justification: The operational knowledge-boundary definition and mathematical content of Equations 1–5 and the baseline equations remain equivalent. Changes to locality notation and the added parametric-knowledge discussion are clarifications, with no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: generation-free query-level uncertainty, training-free Internal Confidence, favorable accuracy–cost tradeoffs, and applications to adaptive RAG and cascading. Terminology changes and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly identifies incompatibility with fully black-box APIs and acknowledges weaker performance than answer-level approaches, while expanding discussion of task-dependent decision centers. Section 4.3 changes its accuracy interpretation from state-of-the-art to competitive. Conversely, Appendix D.1 replaces v2's acknowledgment of overlapping confidence distributions with stronger separation and seen/unseen-input interpretations, despite retaining Figure A1.

D1.justification: New Appendix B supplies the complete self-assessment prompt template, extending the illustrative prompt already present in Section 3.2. Appendix D.4 documents TruthfulQA center selection and selected layers 9, 7, and 23 for Phi, Llama, and Qwen. The code-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.4 adds substantive positioning against adaptive RAG methods requiring training or answer generation, with six additional citations. Section 3.2 adds Slobodkin et al. on hidden-state answerability, alongside references supporting new comparators and datasets. The principal related-work structure and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Targeted edits replace known/unknown with answerable/non-answerable, clarify AUROC terminology and locality notation, and expand explanations of greedy decoding and self-assessment. Limitations and prompt sections are added, and appendix sections are renumbered. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1a adds comparator points and revises its axis display; Figure 2 adds explicit answerability branches. Tables 2 and A1 expand, while Table A2 and three multi-panel heatmap figures are new. Existing plots are largely retained or relocated. The new heatmap captions conflict with their model panel labels.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, broader benchmark and comparator evidence, explicit applicability limitations, and a fuller prompt description make v4 more informative and reproducible. These gains are limited by unresolved inconsistencies: TruthfulQA requires learned tuning despite the general training-free framing, Section 4.3 still calls 66.8 the best AUROC although MSP achieves 68.5, and the new heatmap captions obscure attribution.
